week_1.text:
We just shipped something most ad platforms won't build for years.

Synter now has a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server — meaning any AI agent (Claude, Cursor, Amp) can manage your ad campaigns across 7 platforms through a single interface.

What that looks like in practice:

→ Ask Claude to pull your Google Ads performance
→ Have it pause underperforming Meta campaigns
→ Reallocate budget to your best LinkedIn ad sets
→ Generate fresh creatives with Imagen 4
→ Launch everything — without opening a single dashboard

The MCP server handles OAuth credential injection, credit billing, user scoping, and audit logging automatically. Your AI agent just talks to Synter, and Synter executes.

Platforms supported today:
• Google Ads
• Meta (Facebook/Instagram)
• LinkedIn Ads
• Reddit Ads
• X Ads
• TikTok Ads

This is what we mean by AI Agent Media Buyers. Not a chatbot bolted onto a dashboard. An actual execution layer that turns conversation into live campaigns.

week_1.text:
The average media buyer manages 3-4 platforms manually.

They log into Google Ads. Pull a report. Switch to Meta. Pull another report. Open a spreadsheet. Compare numbers. Make a decision. Go back to each platform. Adjust bids. Repeat.

That workflow takes 6-8 hours per week — and it's fundamentally reactive. By the time you've analyzed yesterday's data across platforms, the opportunity has already moved.

Here's the shift happening right now:

AI agents don't context-switch. They don't forget to check Reddit Ads because the Meta dashboard was on fire. They don't deprioritize TikTok because the LinkedIn campaign needed attention.

An AI agent pulls performance from all 7 platforms simultaneously. It identifies the cross-platform pattern — "LinkedIn CPL dropped 22% while Google CPA rose 15% on the same audience" — and acts on it in minutes, not days.

This isn't about replacing media buyers. It's about giving them agents that handle the execution while they focus on strategy.

The teams that figure this out first will operate at a fundamentally different speed than everyone else.

week_1.text:
March build update — shipping faster than ever.

What we deployed in the last 30 days:

→ Reddit Ads v3 API integration (full campaign lifecycle — create, pause, update, report)
→ Fixed Reddit OAuth PKCE issue that silently broke refresh tokens
→ X Growth Engine — pay-per-usage ads API support (~$0.01/post)
→ TikTok Events API (CAPI) for server-side conversion tracking
→ Microsoft Ads offline conversions
→ Granular OAuth connection UX with 10-stage progress tracking
→ Custom Nango Docker image with provider-specific PKCE patches

The hardest bug this month: Reddit's OAuth endpoint silently drops your refresh_token when PKCE code_challenge is present — even with duration=permanent. No error. No warning. Your connection just dies after 60 minutes.

We patched our Nango instance to disable PKCE for Reddit specifically. Took 3 days to diagnose, 4 lines to fix.

Building ad platform integrations is 20% feature work and 80% debugging undocumented API behavior.

More coming next week.

week_2.text:
Here's how Synter manages a $50/day Google Ads campaign from a single chat message.

The prompt: "Create a search campaign for SaaS lead gen targeting marketing automation keywords with a $50 daily budget."

What Synter does in under 90 seconds:

1. Creates the campaign with all Google Ads API v21 required fields (including EU political advertising flag, explicit network settings)
2. Sets bidding to maximize_clicks (no conversion data yet — Synter knows not to use maximize_conversions without tracking)
3. Generates keyword groups from the prompt
4. Creates responsive search ads with 15 headlines and 4 descriptions
5. Sets geo-targeting
6. Launches in PAUSED state for review

Then, without being asked:

→ Creates a Google Ads conversion action
→ Sets up the GTM tag with the conversion label
→ Publishes the GTM container
→ Recommends switching to maximize_conversions after 15-30 conversions

No dashboard hopping. No copy-pasting conversion IDs between tabs. No forgetting to publish the GTM container (we've all done it).

Synter handles the full lifecycle because it understands the dependencies between tracking, bidding, and creative.

That's what AI Agent Media Buyers actually means.

week_3.text:
We track conversion events across 7 platforms simultaneously. Here's how.

When someone signs up on syntermedia.ai, a single function fires server-side events to:

• Meta CAPI (SHA-256 hashed email + fbclid + fbc cookie)
• Google Ads (gclid + enhanced conversions)
• Reddit CAPI (rdt_cid + _rdt_uuid cookie)
• LinkedIn CAPI (li_fat_id + conversion_rule_id)
• X Conversion API (twclid)
• TikTok Events API (ttclid + _ttp cookie)
• Microsoft Ads (msclkid + hashed PII)

All 7 calls fire in parallel. Deduplication handled by a shared conversion_id.

Our middleware captures every click ID from URL parameters — gclid, fbclid, rdt_cid, li_fat_id, twclid, ttclid, msclkid — stores them in first-party cookies, and passes them through the entire funnel.

Why server-side? Browser privacy changes (ITP, cookie restrictions, ad blockers) drop 20-40% of client-side conversion events. Server-side tracking recovers most of that.

We built this for ourselves first. Now every Synter user gets the same infrastructure automatically when they connect their ad accounts.

The tracking code nobody wants to write is the tracking code that matters most.

From competitor insight to live campaign in a single conversation.

This isn't about copying ads. It's about understanding what's working in your market and responding faster than manual teams can.

week_4.text:
Synter generates video ads with Veo and launches them as YouTube campaigns — from a single prompt.

The workflow:

→ You describe the video concept in chat
→ Synter generates an 8-second video using Google's Veo model
→ Video is uploaded to YouTube automatically
→ A Demand Gen campaign is created targeting custom intent audiences
→ Headlines, descriptions, and business name are set
→ Geo-targeting and budget are configured
→ Campaign launches in PAUSED state for your review

Why Demand Gen and not a Video campaign? Because Google's Ads API doesn't support creating Video campaigns programmatically. It only supports reporting on existing ones.

Demand Gen campaigns serve video ads on YouTube, YouTube Shorts, Discover, and Gmail — covering the same inventory with full API support.

Synter knows these API limitations and routes around them automatically. You don't need to know that the Video campaign type is report-only. You just say "promote this on YouTube" and Synter picks the right campaign type.

That's the difference between a dashboard and an agent.

This is exactly what we're building at Synter.

Not another ad platform. Not another dashboard. An execution layer that works FOR advertisers, across ALL platforms, with zero inventory bias.

The next generation of media buying isn't happening inside any single platform. It's happening above all of them.
